Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 77, verses 1–7:

Naming of the surah

• It is called al-Mursalat (Those Sent Forth), because it opens with Allah's oath by "al-Mursalat," which are the winds.

The aims of the surah

• Proving that resurrection occurs right after the end of this world; mentioning some of the attributes of that Day; mentioning the evidence of Allah's power to restore humankind after death; alluding to punishment for those who denied in this world; explaining their fate in the Hereafter; speaking of the righteous believers in contrast to them; and mentioning what Allah has prepared for them of various kinds of honor.

[The Tafsir]

Allah the Exalted swears by the winds when they blow in succession, one following another, and by the violently blowing winds that destroy, and by the angels entrusted with the clouds, driving them wherever Allah wills, and by the angels that descend from Allah with that which distinguishes between truth and falsehood, and lawful and unlawful, and by the angels that receive revelation from Allah and bring it down to His prophets, as an excuse from Allah to His creation and a warning from Him to them, so that they will have no argument. Indeed, what you are promised of the matter of the Day of Resurrection, with its reckoning and recompense, is surely going to befall you without doubt.

It will be said: "For what day have the Messengers been delayed? They have been delayed until the Day of Decision and Judgment among all creatures." And what will make you know, O human being, what the Day of Decision is, and how severe and terrifying it is? Woe on that Day to those who denied this promised day.

The Noble Qur'an (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar), commentary on Surah 77, verses 29–33:

It will be said to the disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection: "Proceed to the punishment of Hell, which you used to deny in the world. Proceed, and seek shade in the smoke of Hell, which branches out into three columns, a shade that will neither shelter from the heat of that Day nor avail against the blaze of the flame." Indeed, Hell throws out sparks of great size, each spark like a towering palace in its bulk and height. It is as though the sparks flying from it were yellowish-black camels.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 77, verses 41–45:

Indeed, those who feared their Lord in the world and guarded themselves against His punishment by carrying out His commands and avoiding His prohibitions, they will be on the Day of Resurrection in the shade of spreading trees and among flowing springs, and with abundant fruits of whatever their souls desire, enjoying delights. It will be said to them: "Eat with pleasant enjoyment, and drink with wholesome satisfaction, because of what you sent forward in the world of good deeds." Indeed, it is with such a great reward that We recompense the people of excellence (ihsan) for their deeds and their obedience to Us. Woe and severe punishment on the Day of Resurrection to those who deny the Day of Recompense and Reckoning, and what it contains of bliss and punishment.

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 77, verse 48:
